runtime.command_template: python tools/run_pinmame_harness.py --library <libpinmame> --game ft_l5 --rom-path <vpinmame-roms> --work-dir <new-isolated-state> --handle-mechanics 0 --scenario tools/harness-scenarios/wpc-fliptronic/ft-switch-edges-37-38-47-48.json --dmd-dir <external-dmd-dir> --output <external-run.json>. Built-in mechanisms stay disabled because ft_handleMech would overwrite 48 (mech 0x01) and 37/38 (mech 0x02). Each set_switch holds one public level for 2 s; the snapshot after it records the ROM's T.1 display, its switch grid and the watched public switch levels.

named_action_observations.label: public 41 (ordinary switch) set to 1 inside T.1 SWITCH EDGES: the ROM's top line names it (CAPTIVE BALL), so the ROM reads public 41 = 1 as active; the switch grid marks its closed matrix contact
public 41 (ordinary switch) set to 0 inside T.1 SWITCH EDGES: the ROM's top line returns to SWITCH EDGES, so the ROM reads public 0 as inactive

public 47 (printed microswitch, outside the inverted-switch mask) set to 1 inside T.1 SWITCH EDGES: the ROM's top line names it (BALL POPPER), so the ROM reads public 47 = 1 as active; the switch grid marks its closed matrix contact
public 47 (printed microswitch, outside the inverted-switch mask) set to 0 inside T.1 SWITCH EDGES: the ROM's top line returns to SWITCH EDGES, so the ROM reads public 0 as inactive

public 48 (printed microswitch, outside the inverted-switch mask) set to 1 inside T.1 SWITCH EDGES: the ROM's top line names it (DROP TARGET), so the ROM reads public 48 = 1 as active; the switch grid marks its closed matrix contact
public 48 (printed microswitch, outside the inverted-switch mask) set to 0 inside T.1 SWITCH EDGES: the ROM's top line returns to SWITCH EDGES, so the ROM reads public 0 as inactive

public 112 (lower-right flipper button in the Fliptronic column, which PinMAME complements as a whole) set to 1 inside T.1 SWITCH EDGES: the ROM fires the right flipper (public 46), PinMAME's end-of-stroke simulation raises public 111 to 1 and the ROM's top line names R FLIPPER EOS (F1), the last contact to close; this shows the ROM reads public 112 = 1 as the pressed button, and is not an opto-logic control because PinMAME inverts that whole column

public 112 (lower-right flipper button in the Fliptronic column, which PinMAME complements as a whole) set to 0 inside T.1 SWITCH EDGES: public 46 and 111 fall back to 0 and the ROM's top line returns to SWITCH EDGES

public 37 (printed opto, inverted by ftGameData's mask) set to 0 inside T.1 SWITCH EDGES: the ROM's top line names it (REEL 1 OPTO), so the ROM reads public 37 = 0 as active; through ftGameData's mask public 0 is the closed matrix contact, which the switch grid marks

public 37 (printed opto, inverted by ftGameData's mask) set to 1 inside T.1 SWITCH EDGES: the ROM's top line stays at or returns to SWITCH EDGES, so the ROM reads public 37 = 1 as inactive; the grid mark clears because the matrix contact is open

public 38 (printed opto, inverted by ftGameData's mask) set to 0 inside T.1 SWITCH EDGES: the ROM's top line names it (REEL 2 OPTO), so the ROM reads public 38 = 0 as active; through ftGameData's mask public 0 is the closed matrix contact, which the switch grid marks

public 38 (printed opto, inverted by ftGameData's mask) set to 1 inside T.1 SWITCH EDGES: the ROM's top line stays at or returns to SWITCH EDGES, so the ROM reads public 38 = 1 as inactive; the grid mark clears because the matrix contact is open
